cells.tense: You are holding the shape right now and it is setting without strain.
cells.ask: Give one piece of a structure you hold to someone who wants to run with it, and leave the shape of that piece to them.
cells.core:
You can carry a weight and stay soft around it. The plan holds, the people in it can move, and nothing has to be crushed to keep the thing upright. When a piece wants to shift, you feel it before it breaks, and you adjust rather than brace. That is the trick, and not a small one.

Here is where the company is. You can feel your way into what someone else needs without taking their load or dropping yours. Someone stays steadier at their work because of how you hold yours, and you let that land as something between you. Notice it while the floor is still under it. That recognition is the part of this that has somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the shape without gripping it, and that is working.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get made

cells.tense: You are bracing for something that has not happened yet, tightening before it arrives.
cells.ask: Find one place you have tightened past what the task needs, and loosen it enough that the next person can move too.
cells.core:
You are gripping the structure harder than it needs to be held. You set the shape and then stand over it, watching for a crack that is not there. Every rule gets enforced ahead of its need, every plan braced against a future you cannot write in yet. From the outside, the strength has started to look like stiffness.

What is missing is not strength. It is the plain question of what is fair to the thing you are holding and to the people inside it. Let one piece run on what the moment actually asks, not on every failure you can imagine. You may find the structure holds without your shoulder pressing on it. That is worth knowing on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You have tightened past what the thing needs.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get made

cells.tense: You are not picking up the load in front of you, and the room shows it.
cells.ask: Pick one piece of structure already started, finish it today, and stop when it is done without adding anything more.
cells.core:
The structure you could keep standing is not being picked up. Reaching for it reads as the first step into collapse, so the work happens around you and you stay back from it. The strength has not gone anywhere. It stays out of sight because holding anything looks like it would ask more than you have.

The move is not to brace harder. Finish one small thing you already began, let it be complete, and stop there. When a piece is done, setting it down is its own kind of strength, not a defeat. Start with something that has a clean edge. Getting to the finish is the point, not the size of the thing.
cells.sheetLine: You can put one thing down by finishing it first.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get made

cells.tense: You are already holding more than you would ever claim to be holding.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are holding steady, out loud or in writing, as yours before anyone asks.
cells.core:
People around you organize their days by the shape you keep, and you would describe your part as sitting on the sidelines. The steadying happens through you whether or not you call it yours. You keep looking ahead at the person you want to be and missing the structural work already standing under the people near you.

Somebody says out loud that the thing held, and you hear that it was your hand. The pull toward a better version is real, and it points at something already in view. Claim one piece of it while the feeling is still warm. What is shining is yours even before you say so.
cells.sheetLine: You are already holding this steady. You just call it waiting.
cells.place: where pattern and structure get made

A reader could say the structure is a job and not theirs to author, which is why the asks are acts anyone could do inside a role and survive being wrong. The sentence that serves me is 'you build the thing that holds,' a line the record has not earned; I have cut it.
